turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name]. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?
turns.patient_response:
Well, hi Doctor. I suppose I'm here because of my job. I work as a cashier, and, well, things have been getting really complicated for me at the register lately. It’s a bit hard to explain, but I keep getting... stuck, I guess you could say. 

I'll be in the middle of ringing someone up—just a normal transaction, maybe they have a few items, some groceries, nothing out of the ordinary—and suddenly I find myself doing these things that just really don’t fit the moment at all. For example, I’ll start tapping the barcode scanner on the edge of the counter in this very specific pattern, just tap-tap-tapping it, instead of actually scanning the next item. I don't really know why, it's just what happens. 

Or, and this is what really caused a major problem the other day, I'll just freeze completely. I had the cash drawer pop open after I totaled the order, and my hand was just hovering right there over the bills, and I just froze. I couldn't move it. The customer was standing right in front of me, just waiting for their change, shifting from foot to foot, looking at me like I was crazy, and I was just stuck there with my hand in the air over the drawer. It's so frustrating because I know they're waiting, and I know how to do my job—I mean, I have a bachelor's degree, the math is certainly not the issue—but I just get caught in these moments where my body just stops or repeats things. 

And because of all that, my manager actually pulled me aside into the back office last week and I got written up. They had the whole official form and everything, talking about productivity and customer complaints, and it's just... it's really stressful because I need to keep this job, you know? So I figured I had to come in and see if someone could help me figure out why I keep getting stuck like that.

It's completely out of my control, which is exactly what I tried to explain to my manager when he pulled me into the office.
